tasks.objective: Run the bounded probe (30-60 min cap): enumerate ALL external readers of config.json by grepping the repo for references to 'config.json', inspecting CI config and deploy scripts, and reading the deploy runbook where present; record the complete reader list (each reader with location + evidence) and a route A vs B recommendation as a plan artifact.

concepts: route A (keep JSON export mirror) vs route B (full cutover) decision criteria from the task input
required config keys (C2) that each reader may depend on

forbidden_scope: app/ (read-only for the spike — no code changes)
adding dependencies, code, or config keys
outputs: spike-reader-inventory.md: complete reader list with per-reader evidence + explicit route recommendation with reasoning
tasks.split_rationale: evidence-gathering closure: grep + script/runbook reads with no code context shared with the store implementation; separate so the route decision rests on evidence, not implementer assumption, and it has a hard 30-60 min boundary

tasks.objective: Implement YamlConfigStore in app/yaml_store.py satisfying the frozen C1 store interface (get/set/save/as_dict, REQUIRED_KEYS, ConfigError on missing file) over a vendored YAML-subset parser (flat dict of scalars, stdlib only), and prove full behavioral parity with JsonConfigStore via a parity test matrix in tests/test_yaml_store.py; loader.py and cli.py stay on JSON (DA-1).

concepts: YAML-subset parse/serialize for flat scalar maps
interface parity testing against a reference implementation

forbidden_scope: app/loader.py and app/cli.py (DA-1: unwired in this stage)
tasks.split_rationale: store implementation + its parity suite is one closure: both share the C1 interface, the config_store.py reference, and the test matrix; splitting implementation from tests would make both agents re-learn the same interface (pure context amplification), and the work stays within two layers with no stable seam to cut
